title: Single-shot state preparation threshold: rigorous theorem and statistical mechanical mapping
authors: Yuanchen Zhao, Yi Yuan, Zhengyi Han, Dong E. Liu
abstract: Preparing logical codewords with a single round of noisy syndrome measurements can reduce the time overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation. It remains unclear which structural properties of the code suffice to guarantee a threshold for single-shot state preparation. Here we prove that linear confinement suffices for a nonzero single-shot state-preparation threshold for CSS quantum low-density parity-check codes, in contrast to the common belief that soundness is necessary. When the distance is at least logarithmic, we prove that below nonzero local stochastic readout and data error thresholds, the logical error probability after a formal ideal final recovery is exponentially small and approaches zero when the code size approaches infinity. Under the stronger assumption of linear soundness, we show that the residual data error of the preparation protocol is local stochastic, directly allowing composition with other fault-tolerant gadgets. To investigate single-shot state-preparation threshold beyond the above assumptions, we further develop a statistical mechanical mapping that expresses the final logical error rate in terms of a classical partition function. We perform Monte Carlo simulations of this model for the three-dimensional toric code. The numerical results suggest that sublinear soundness can also support a single-shot state-preparation threshold.
summary: This paper establishes new, weaker structural conditions—specifically linear confinement—that are sufficient to guarantee a non-zero threshold for single-shot state preparation in quantum error correcting codes. By developing a statistical mechanical mapping, the authors provide a powerful tool to analyze the logical error rate, suggesting that even sublinear soundness might suffice for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental question of determining the threshold for performing single-shot state preparation in Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes.
main_result: It proves that linear confinement, a structural property, is sufficient for a nonzero single-shot state-preparation threshold for CSS qLDPC codes, contradicting the prior belief that full soundness is necessary.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical proofs, developing a statistical mechanical mapping to relate the logical error rate to a classical partition function, and employing Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on CSS quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes and the process of preparing logical codewords using only a single round of noisy syndrome measurements.
key_observables: Logical error probability ($P_{	ext{fail}}$), residual data error, and the structure of the error channel $\mathcal{S}$.
important_parameters: Code distance ($d$), error parameters ($p, q$), and structural properties like linear confinement and linear soundness.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the state preparation is followed by an ideal final recovery, and the statistical mapping relies on maximum-likelihood final recovery.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the necessary preliminaries for CSS codes, then presents the main threshold theorem based on structural properties (soundness vs. confinement), and concludes with the development and application of a statistical mechanical mapping.
why_interesting: The work provides concrete, structural conditions (linear confinement) that guarantee fault-tolerance thresholds, which is crucial for designing practical, resource-efficient quantum computation protocols.

Panels (a,b) show noiseless readout, q = 0, while panels (c,d) include readout errors with q = p/10, where p and q are the data and readout error probabilities, respectively. At lower noise, increasing the system size suppresses the logical error rate after ideal maximum-likelihood final recovery (left) and increases the logical-sector order parameter [qtop]dis (right); both size dependences reverse at higher noise. The persistence of these crossings at nonzero readout noise supports a single-shot preparation threshold even with sublinear soundness....
